mechanism_narrative: A strong increase in GDP growth rate indicates a robust economy, leading to higher consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong GDP growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 1.5%, it signals a tightening monetary cycle, leading to decreased borrowing and spending, and ultimately resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline when the federal funds rate is above 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate indicates a weakening labor market, leading to decreased consumer spending and subsequently driving down the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods of rising unemployment (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates a strong supply chain, leading to increased economic growth and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods of strong industrial production growth (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts increase and the federal funds rate is below 1%, it signals a strong demand for housing and a supportive monetary policy, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 10% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 1%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when housing starts are increasing and the federal funds rate is below 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate and an increase in the consumer price index indicates an expansionary monetary policy and increased inflation, leading to increased borrowing and spending, and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.5pp in 2 months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when the federal funds rate is decreasing and the consumer price index is increasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in payroll employment and a decrease in the unemployment rate indicates a strong labor market, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 1% in 3 months and UNRATE falls < 0.5pp in 2 months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when payroll employment is increasing and the unemployment rate is decreasing (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When retail sales increase and the federal funds rate is below 1.5%, it signals a strong demand for consumer goods and a supportive monetary policy, leading to increased consumer spending and subsequently driving up the S&P 500 index over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS rises > 5% in 3 months and FEDFUNDS < 1.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline when retail sales are increasing and the federal funds rate is below 1.5% (t-test p > 0.05).
